result.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
result.summary: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用带偏置校正 EMA 动量的 bandit 形式分析 RLVR 中一阶动量何时加速优化，给出 β 与学习率耦合的理论条件，并在 Qwen3-4B-Base、Qwen2.5-32B 的 RLVR 实验中验证增大 β₁ 的收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及视觉或多模态状态，但其关于 RLVR 训练优化器中动量系数与学习率关系的结论，可能为 LVR 模型 RL 微调阶段的超参设置与训练稳定性提供可供核查的方法线索。
